sources.title: Louisiana Withholding Tables and Formulas R-1306

calculation.supplementalWages: Supplemental and vacation pay are subject to withholding using the same method as regular payroll even when paid separately.

residencyAndWorkRules.louisianaServices: Withhold from resident and nonresident employees for services performed in Louisiana unless specifically exempt.
residencyAndWorkRules.residentOtherStateWithIncomeTax: Withhold the work state's tax; Louisiana resident reports all income and may claim a return-level credit for tax paid to the other state.
residencyAndWorkRules.residentOtherStateWithoutIncomeTax: Louisiana withholding is required from the Louisiana resident's wages earned in the no-tax state.

captureWarnings: The shared source index previously summarized the rate as 3%; the official formula is 3.09%, so the individual capture intentionally corrects that reference value.

The formula publication is effective January 1, 2025 and the agency identifies it as the current table while issuing a January 2026 L-4; uninterrupted applicability for every 2026 payroll still requires independent sign-off.
The official second example prints $112.432 and does not state a generalized rounding sequence; executable behavior must resolve final-cent rounding.
The full wage-bracket matrices are retained in the checksummed publication and are not duplicated here.

review.requiredNextStep: Confirm the current R-1306 applies to every 2026 payroll, import wage-bracket matrices, verify adjustment and rounding behavior, and add executable residency and formula tests before activation.
